title: International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise
publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
claims: An overall daily protein intake of 1.4-2.0 g/kg body weight per day is sufficient for most exercising individuals.
General per-serving recommendations are about 0.25 g of high-quality protein per kg body weight, or an absolute dose of 20-40 g, distributed every 3-4 hours across the day.
Physically active people can meet protein needs with whole foods, while supplements can be a practical way to ensure adequate intake.
Endurance athletes should focus on adequate carbohydrate intake for performance; protein may help offset muscle damage and support recovery.

verification.note: 已读 PMC 全文（Europe PMC XML），position stand 各条原文逐句核对。

claimVerification.note: 原文：“For building muscle mass and for maintaining muscle mass through a positive muscle protein balance, an overall daily protein intake in the range of 1.4–2.0 g protein/kg body weight/day (g/kg/d) is sufficient for most exercising individuals”。数字一致；原文把这句限定在“增肌/维持肌肉量”的目的下，claim 省略了该前提。

原文：“General recommendations are 0.25 g of a high-quality protein per kg of body weight, or an absolute dose of 20–40 g”；“These protein doses should ideally be evenly distributed, every 3–4 h, across the day.”

原文：“While it is possible for physically active individuals to obtain their daily protein requirements through the consumption of whole foods, supplementation is a practical way of ensuring intake of adequate protein quality and quantity”。
原文：“Endurance athletes should focus on achieving adequate carbohydrate intake to promote optimal performance; the addition of protein may help to offset muscle damage and promote recovery.”
